subject.title: [Feature]: cron add: support custom job IDs via --id

question: Should OpenClaw expose user-supplied cron job IDs at create time, and what validation plus agent-tool scope should be the public contract?
rationale: This is not a broken existing contract; it adds a persisted user-controlled identifier to a public cron CLI/Gateway/API creation path, so automation should not choose the permanent contract without maintainer direction.

options.title: Approve create-time custom IDs
options.body: Add an explicit optional create id with conservative validation, duplicate rejection, docs/tests, generated-client updates, and unchanged UUID behavior when omitted.

options.title: Limit to display and discoverability
options.body: Keep generated IDs as the only create contract and improve listing, UI, docs, or copy flows so operators can work with existing IDs more easily.

options.title: Defer to broader cron API design
options.body: Keep this issue open but block implementation until cron storage/API naming and declarative-job direction are settled together.

recommendation.title: Approve create-time custom IDs
recommendation.body: Add an explicit optional create id with conservative validation, duplicate rejection, docs/tests, generated-client updates, and unchanged UUID behavior when omitted.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history signal on the cron scheduler/create path and broad adjacent ownership context for a public cron contract decision.
